13.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, and no sentence over 14 words (sentence-length pass 2026-11-23). V32-33 keep the KJV's evil report and giants.

verses.text: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
Send men, so that they may search (explore) the land of Canaan. I give it to the children of Israel. Send a man of every tribe of their fathers. Every one shall be a ruler (leader) among them.
And Moses sent them from the wilderness (desert) of Paran. He did it by the commandment of the LORD. All those men were heads (leaders) of the children of Israel.
And these were their names: Of the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the son of Zaccur.
Of the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori.
Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph.
Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun.
Of the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu.
Of the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi.
Of the tribe of Joseph, that is, of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi.
Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli.
Of the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael.
Of the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi.
Of the tribe of Gad, Geuel the son of Machi.
These are the names of the men Moses sent to spy out the land. And Moses called Oshea the son of Nun Jehoshua (Joshua).
And Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan. He said to them: Go up this way southward, and go up into the mountain.
And see the land, what it is. See the people that dwell (live) in it. See whether they are strong or weak, few or many.
See what the land is that they dwell (live) in. See whether it is good or bad. See what cities they dwell in. See whether they live in tents, or in strong holds (forts).

See what the land is, whether it is fat or lean (rich or poor soil). See whether there is wood in it, or not. And be of good courage (be brave), and bring of the fruit of the land. Now the time was the time of the firstripe (first ripe) grapes.
So they went up, and searched (explored) the land. They went from the wilderness (desert) of Zin to Rehob, as men come to Hamath.
And they went up by the south, and came to Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of Anak, were there. (Now Hebron was built 7 years before Zoan in Egypt.)

And they came to the brook (stream) of Eshcol. They cut down from there a branch with one cluster (bunch) of grapes. And they bare (carried) it between 2 men upon a staff (pole). And they brought some of the pomegranates, and of the figs.
The place was called the brook (stream) Eshcol (cluster). It was because of the cluster (bunch) of grapes there. The children of Israel cut it down from there.
And they returned from searching (exploring) the land after 40 days.

And they went and came to Moses, and to Aaron. They came to all the congregation (people) of the children of Israel. They came to the wilderness (desert) of Paran, to Kadesh. And they brought back word to them, and to all the congregation (people). And they showed them the fruit of the land.
And they told Moses, and said: We came to the land where you sent us. And surely it flows with milk and honey. And this is the fruit of it.
Nevertheless (but) the people that dwell (live) in the land are strong. And the cities are walled, and very great. And moreover (also) we saw the children of Anak there.

The Amalekites dwell (live) in the land of the south. And the Hittites, and the Jebusites, and the Amorites, dwell in the mountains. And the Canaanites dwell by the sea, and by the coast (side) of the Jordan.
And Caleb stilled (quieted) the people before Moses, and said: Let us go up at once, and possess (take) it. For we are well able to overcome (win against) it.
But the men that went up with Caleb said: We are not able to go up against the people. For they are stronger than we are.

And they brought up an evil (bad) report of the land to Israel. It was the land which they had searched (explored). They said: We have gone through the land. It is a land that eats up the inhabitants (people living there). All the people that we saw in it are men of great stature (very tall).
And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak. They come from the giants. And we were in our own sight as grasshoppers. And so we were in their sight.

14.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, and no sentence over 14 words (sentence-length pass 2026-11-23). V44 writes the ark of the covenant as the ark (holy box) of the agreement, as elsewhere on the site.

verses.text: And all the congregation (people) lifted up their voice, and cried. And the people wept that night.

And all the children of Israel murmured (complained) against Moses and against Aaron. And the whole congregation (all the people) said to them: Would God that we had died in the land of Egypt! Or would God we had died in this wilderness (desert)!
Wherefore (why) has the LORD brought us to this land, to fall by the sword? Our wives and our children will be a prey (captured). Would it not be better for us to return into Egypt?
And they said one to another: Let us make a captain (leader), and let us return into Egypt.
Then Moses and Aaron fell on their faces. They fell before all the assembly of the children of Israel.
And Joshua the son of Nun rent (tore) his clothes. Caleb the son of Jephunneh tore his clothes too. They were among those who searched (explored) the land.
And they spoke to all the company of the children of Israel, saying: We passed through the land to search (explore) it. It is an exceeding (very) good land.
If the LORD delight in (is pleased with) us, then He will bring us into this land. He will give it to us. It is a land which flows with milk and honey.

Only do not rebel against the LORD. And do not fear the people of the land. For they are bread for us (we will easily win). Their defence (protection) is departed (gone) from them, and the LORD is with us. Fear them not.
But all the congregation (people) said to stone them with stones. And the glory of the LORD appeared in the tabernacle (holy tent) of the congregation. It appeared before all the children of Israel.
And the LORD said to Moses: How long will this people provoke (anger) Me? How long will it be ere (before) they believe Me? I have showed many signs among them.
I will smite (strike) them with the pestilence (deadly disease), and disinherit (take away their land from) them. And I will make of you a greater nation and mightier than they.
And Moses said to the LORD: Then the Egyptians shall hear it. (For You brought up this people in Your might from among them.)

And they will tell it to the inhabitants (people) of this land. For they have heard that You, LORD, are among this people. They have heard that You, LORD, are seen face to face. They heard that Your cloud stands over them. You go before them by day time in a pillar (tall column) of a cloud. And You go before them in a pillar of fire by night.
Now You may kill all this people as one man. Then the nations which have heard the fame of You will speak, saying:
The LORD was not able to bring this people into the land. He sware (promised) it to them. Therefore He has slain (killed) them in the wilderness (desert).
And now, I beseech (beg) You, let the power of my LORD be great. Let it be as You have spoken, saying:

The LORD is longsuffering (patient), and of great mercy. He forgives iniquity (sin) and transgression (breaking the law). He by no means clears the guilty. He visits (punishes) the iniquity of the fathers upon the children. He punishes it to the 3rd and 4th generation.
Pardon (forgive), I beseech (beg) You, the iniquity (sin) of this people. Forgive according to the greatness of Your mercy. Forgive as You have forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.
And the LORD said: I have pardoned (forgiven) according to your word.
But as truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled. It shall be filled with the glory of the LORD.

All those men have seen My glory. They saw My miracles which I did in Egypt. They saw what I did in the wilderness (desert). They have tempted (tested) Me now these 10 times. And they have not hearkened (listened) to My voice.
Surely they shall not see the land which I sware (promised) to their fathers. Neither shall any of those who provoked (angered) Me see it.
But My servant Caleb had another spirit with him, and has followed Me fully. Him will I bring into the land where he went. And his seed (children) shall possess (own) it.
(Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites dwelt (lived) in the valley.) To morrow (tomorrow) turn. Go into the wilderness (desert) by the way of the Red sea.
And the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying:
How long shall I bear with this evil congregation (group), which murmur (complain) against Me? I have heard the murmurings (complaints) of the children of Israel. They murmur against Me.
Say to them: As truly as I live, says the LORD, I will do this. As you have spoken in My ears, so will I do to you.

Your carcases (dead bodies) shall fall in this wilderness (desert). All of you that were numbered (counted) shall fall. All from 20 years old and upward shall fall. They have murmured (complained) against Me.
Doubtless (surely) you shall not come into the land. I sware (promised) to make you dwell (live) there. Only Caleb the son of Jephunneh shall come, and Joshua the son of Nun.
But you said your little ones should be a prey (captured). Them will I bring in. And they shall know the land which you have despised (rejected).
But as for you, your carcases (dead bodies), they shall fall in this wilderness (desert).

And your children shall wander in the wilderness (desert) 40 years. They shall bear your whoredoms (suffer for your unfaithfulness). It will last until your carcases (dead bodies) be wasted in the wilderness.

You searched (explored) the land for 40 days. Each day shall be for a year. So you shall bear (suffer for) your iniquities (sins) 40 years. And you shall know My breach of promise (what it is when I turn against you).

I the LORD have said it. I will surely do it to all this evil congregation (group). They are gathered together against Me. In this wilderness (desert) they shall be consumed (destroyed), and there they shall die.
Moses sent men to search (explore) the land. They returned, and made all the congregation (people) murmur (complain) against Moses. They did it by bringing up a slander (lie) upon the land.
Those men that did bring up the evil (bad) report upon the land died. They died by the plague before the LORD.
But Joshua the son of Nun lived still (stayed alive). Caleb the son of Jephunneh lived too. They were of the men that went to search (explore) the land.
And Moses told these sayings to all the children of Israel. And the people mourned greatly.
And they rose up early in the morning. They gat (went) up into the top of the mountain, saying: Lo (look), we are here. We will go up to the place which the LORD has promised. For we have sinned.
And Moses said: Wherefore (why) now do you transgress (break) the commandment of the LORD? But it shall not prosper (succeed).
Go not up, for the LORD is not among you. Then you will not be smitten (struck down) before your enemies.
For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there before you. And you shall fall by the sword. You are turned away from the LORD. Therefore the LORD will not be with you.
But they presumed (dared) to go up to the hill top. Nevertheless (but) the ark (holy box) of the LORD's agreement departed (went) not out of the camp. And Moses departed not out of the camp.
Then the Amalekites came down, and the Canaanites which dwelt (lived) in that hill. They smote (struck) them, and discomfited (defeated) them, even to Hormah.

16.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, and no sentence over 14 words (sentence-length pass 2026-11-23). Verses 36-50 (the censers made into altar plates, and Aaron standing between the dead and the living) were missing and have been restored. V30 and v33 keep the KJV's pit.

verses.text: Now Korah was the son of Izhar. Izhar was the son of Kohath, the son of Levi. And Dathan and Abiram were the sons of Eliab. And On was the son of Peleth. They were sons of Reuben. They took men.
And they rose up before Moses, with certain of the children of Israel. There were 250 princes (leaders) of the assembly. They were famous in the congregation (people), men of renown (well known).

And they gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, and said to them: You take too much upon you. All the congregation (people) are holy, every one of them. And the LORD is among them. Wherefore (why) then do you lift yourselves up above the congregation of the LORD?
And when Moses heard it, he fell upon his face.

And Moses spoke to Korah and to all his company (group), saying: Even to morrow (tomorrow) the LORD will show who are His. He will show who is holy. And He will cause him to come near to Him. Even him whom He has chosen will He cause to come near to Him.
Do this: Take censers (fire pans), Korah, and all his company (group).
And put fire in them. Put incense (sweet-smelling spice) in them before the LORD to morrow (tomorrow). The man whom the LORD chooses shall be holy. You take too much upon you, you sons of Levi.
And Moses said to Korah: Hear, I pray you (please), you sons of Levi.

Does it seem but a small thing to you? The God of Israel has separated you from the congregation (people) of Israel. He brought you near to Himself. You do the service of the tabernacle (holy tent) of the LORD. You stand before the congregation to minister (serve) to them.
And He has brought you near to Him. All your brethren (brothers) the sons of Levi are with you. And do you seek (want) the priesthood also?
For this cause you and all your company (group) are gathered together against the LORD. And what is Aaron, that you murmur (complain) against him?
And Moses sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab. And they said: We will not come up.

You brought us up out of a land that flows with milk and honey. Is that a small thing? You brought us to kill us in the wilderness (desert). And will you make yourself altogether a prince (ruler) over us?

Moreover (also) you have not brought us into a land of milk and honey. You have not given us inheritance (property) of fields and vineyards. Will you put out the eyes of these men (fool them)? We will not come up.
And Moses was very wroth (angry), and said to the LORD: Respect not (do not accept) their offering. I have not taken one ass (donkey) from them. Neither have I hurt one of them.
And Moses said to Korah: Be you and all your company (group) before the LORD. You, and they, and Aaron, be there to morrow (tomorrow).

And take every man his censer (fire pan), and put incense (sweet-smelling spice) in them. Every man bring his censer before the LORD, 250 censers (fire pans). You also, and Aaron, each of you bring his censer.

And they took every man his censer (fire pan), and put fire in them. They laid incense (sweet-smelling spice) on it. And they stood in the door of the tabernacle (holy tent) of the congregation. Moses and Aaron stood there too.

And Korah gathered all the congregation (people) against them. He gathered them to the door of the tabernacle (holy tent) of the congregation. And the glory of the LORD appeared to all the congregation.
And the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying:
Separate yourselves from among this congregation (group), that I may consume (destroy) them in a moment.
And Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces, and said: O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh (all people)! Shall one man sin? And will You be wroth (angry) with all the congregation (people)?
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to the congregation (people), saying: Get away from around the tabernacle (tent) of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.
And Moses rose up and went to Dathan and Abiram. And the elders of Israel followed him.

And Moses spoke to the congregation (people), saying: Depart (go away), I pray you (please), from the tents of these wicked men. Touch nothing of theirs. Lest (or else) you be consumed (destroyed) in all their sins.

So they got away from the tabernacle (tent) of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram. They left on every side. And Dathan and Abiram came out, and stood in the door of their tents. Their wives, and their sons, and their little children stood there too.
And Moses said: By this you shall know that the LORD has sent me. He sent me to do all these works. For I have not done them of my own mind.
These men may die the common death of all men. What happens to all men may happen to them. Then the LORD has not sent me.

But the LORD may make a new thing. The earth may open her mouth, and swallow them up. It may swallow all that appertain (belong) to them. They may go down quick (alive) into the pit. Then you shall understand that these men have provoked (angered) the LORD.
And it came to pass, as Moses made an end of speaking these words. The ground that was under them clave asunder (split apart).
And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and their houses. It swallowed all the men that appertained (belonged) to Korah, and all their goods.
They, and all that appertained (belonged) to them, went down alive into the pit. And the earth closed upon them. And they perished (died) from among the congregation (people).
And all Israel that were round about them fled (ran) at the cry of them. For they said: Lest (or else) the earth swallow us up also.
And there came out a fire from the LORD. It consumed (burned up) the 250 men that offered incense (sweet-smelling spice).
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
Speak to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest. He must take up the censers (fire pans) out of the burning. And scatter the fire yonder (over there). For they are hallowed (holy).

These sinners sinned against their own souls. Let them make their censers (fire pans) into broad plates. They shall be a covering of the altar. For they offered them before the LORD, therefore they are hallowed (holy). And they shall be a sign to the children of Israel.
And Eleazar the priest took the brasen (bronze) censers (fire pans). Those who were burnt had offered with them. And they were made broad plates for a covering of the altar.

They were to be a memorial (a way to remember) to the children of Israel. No stranger, which is not of the seed (family) of Aaron, may come near. He may not offer incense (sweet-smelling spice) before the LORD. Then he will not be as Korah, and as his company (group). The LORD said this to Eleazar by the hand of Moses.
But on the morrow (next day) all the children of Israel murmured (complained). They murmured against Moses and against Aaron, saying: You have killed the people of the LORD.

And it came to pass, when the people were gathered against Moses and Aaron. They looked toward the tabernacle (holy tent) of the congregation. And look, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
And Moses and Aaron came before the tabernacle (holy tent) of the congregation.
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
Get away from this congregation (group), that I may consume (destroy) them as in a moment. And Moses and Aaron fell upon their faces.

And Moses said to Aaron: Take a censer (fire pan), and put fire in it from off the altar. Put on incense (sweet-smelling spice). Go quickly to the congregation (people), and make an atonement (a covering for sin) for them. For there is wrath (anger) gone out from the LORD. The plague is begun.

And Aaron took as Moses commanded, and ran into the middle of the people. And look, the plague was begun among the people. And Aaron put on incense (sweet-smelling spice). He made an atonement (a covering for sin) for the people.
And Aaron stood between the dead and the living. And the plague was stayed (stopped).
Now those who died in the plague were 14,700. That is beside those who died about the matter of Korah.
And Aaron returned to Moses to the door of the tabernacle (holy tent) of the congregation. And the plague was stayed (stopped).

26.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version (the earlier text was a loose paraphrase), checked against the Hebrew, at a simple, Deaf-friendly reading level with hard KJV words explained in parentheses, and no sentence over 14 words (sentence-length pass 2026-11-23). Population numbers are written as numerals.

verses.text: And it came to pass after the plague. The LORD spoke to Moses and to Eleazar the priest, the son of Aaron. He said:
Take the sum (count) of all the children of Israel. Count those 20 years old and upward. Count them by their fathers' house (family). Count all that are able to go to war in Israel.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab. They were by the Jordan near Jericho. They said:
Take the sum (count) of the people, from 20 years old and upward. Do as the LORD commanded Moses and the children of Israel. They went forth (out) out of the land of Egypt.
Reuben was the eldest (oldest) son of Israel. The children of Reuben: Hanoch, of whom comes the family of the Hanochites. Of Pallu, the family of the Palluites.
Of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites. Of Carmi, the family of the Carmites.
These are the families of the Reubenites. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 43,730.
And the sons of Pallu: Eliab.

And the sons of Eliab: Nemuel, and Dathan, and Abiram. This is that Dathan and Abiram, which were famous in the congregation (people). They strove (fought) against Moses and against Aaron in the company (group) of Korah. They strove against the LORD.

And the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up together with Korah. That was when that company (group) died. At that time the fire devoured (burned up) 250 men. And they became a sign (warning).
Notwithstanding (but) the children of Korah died not.
The sons of Simeon after their families: Of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites. Of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites. Of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites.
Of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites. Of Shaul, the family of the Shaulites.
These are the families of the Simeonites, 22,200.
The children of Gad after their families: Of Zephon, the family of the Zephonites. Of Haggi, the family of the Haggites. Of Shuni, the family of the Shunites.
Of Ozni, the family of the Oznites. Of Eri, the family of the Erites.
Of Arod, the family of the Arodites. Of Areli, the family of the Arelites.
These are the families of the children of Gad. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 40,500.
The sons of Judah were Er and Onan. And Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
And the sons of Judah after their families were: Of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites. Of Pharez, the family of the Pharzites. Of Zerah, the family of the Zarhites.
And the sons of Pharez were: Of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites. Of Hamul, the family of the Hamulites.
These are the families of Judah. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 76,500.
Of the sons of Issachar after their families: Of Tola, the family of the Tolaites. Of Pua, the family of the Punites.
Of Jashub, the family of the Jashubites. Of Shimron, the family of the Shimronites.
These are the families of Issachar. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 64,300.
Of the sons of Zebulun after their families: Of Sered, the family of the Sardites. Of Elon, the family of the Elonites. Of Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites.
These are the families of the Zebulunites. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 60,500.
The sons of Joseph after their families were Manasseh and Ephraim.
Of the sons of Manasseh: Of Machir, the family of the Machirites. And Machir begat (became the father of) Gilead. Of Gilead comes the family of the Gileadites.
These are the sons of Gilead: Of Jeezer, the family of the Jeezerites. Of Helek, the family of the Helekites.
And of Asriel, the family of the Asrielites. And of Shechem, the family of the Shechemites.
And of Shemida, the family of the Shemidaites. And of Hepher, the family of the Hepherites.
And Zelophehad the son of Hepher had no sons, but daughters. The names of the daughters of Zelophehad were Mahlah, and Noah. The others were Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These are the families of Manasseh. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 52,700.
These are the sons of Ephraim after their families: Of Shuthelah, the family of the Shuthalhites. Of Becher, the family of the Bachrites. Of Tahan, the family of the Tahanites.
And these are the sons of Shuthelah: Of Eran, the family of the Eranites.
These are the families of the sons of Ephraim. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 32,500. These are the sons of Joseph after their families.
The sons of Benjamin after their families: Of Bela, the family of the Belaites. Of Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites. Of Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites.
Of Shupham, the family of the Shuphamites. Of Hupham, the family of the Huphamites.
And the sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: Of Ard, the family of the Ardites. And of Naaman, the family of the Naamites.
These are the sons of Benjamin after their families. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 45,600.
These are the sons of Dan after their families: Of Shuham, the family of the Shuhamites. These are the families of Dan after their families.
These are all the families of the Shuhamites. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 64,400.
Of the children of Asher after their families: Of Jimna, the family of the Jimnites. Of Jesui, the family of the Jesuites. Of Beriah, the family of the Beriites.
Of the sons of Beriah: Of Heber, the family of the Heberites. Of Malchiel, the family of the Malchielites.
And the name of the daughter of Asher was Sarah.
These are the families of the sons of Asher. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 53,400.
Of the sons of Naphtali after their families: Of Jahzeel, the family of the Jahzeelites. Of Guni, the family of the Gunites.
Of Jezer, the family of the Jezerites. Of Shillem, the family of the Shillemites.
These are the families of Naphtali according to their families. Those who were numbered (counted) of them were 45,400.
These were the numbered (counted) of the children of Israel, 601,730.
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
To these the land shall be divided for an inheritance (property to keep). It shall be by the number of names.
To many you shall give the more inheritance (property). To few you shall give the less inheritance. Every one shall be given his inheritance by those who were numbered (counted) of him.
Notwithstanding (but) the land shall be divided by lot (drawing lots, a kind of dice). They shall inherit by the names of the tribes of their fathers.
According to the lot (drawing lots) shall the possession (property) be divided between many and few.

And these are those who were numbered (counted) of the Levites after their families: Of Gershon, the family of the Gershonites. Of Kohath, the family of the Kohathites. Of Merari, the family of the Merarites.

These are the families of the Levites: the family of the Libnites, and the family of the Hebronites. There is the family of the Mahlites, and the family of the Mushites. And there is the family of the Korathites. And Kohath begat (became the father of) Amram.

And the name of Amram's wife was Jochebed, the daughter of Levi. Her mother bare (gave birth to) her to Levi in Egypt. And Jochebed bare (gave birth) to Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister.
And to Aaron was born Nadab, and Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
And Nadab and Abihu died, when they offered strange fire (fire God did not command) before the LORD.

And those who were numbered (counted) of them were 23,000. They were all males from a month old and upward. For they were not numbered (counted) among the children of Israel. There was no inheritance (property) given them among the children of Israel.
These are those who were numbered (counted) by Moses and Eleazar the priest. They numbered (counted) the children of Israel in the plains of Moab. They were by the Jordan near Jericho.
But among these there was not a man of the first count. Moses and Aaron the priest numbered (counted) them in the wilderness (desert) of Sinai.
For the LORD had said of them: They shall surely die in the wilderness (desert). And there was not left a man of them. Only Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun, were left.
